prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: ONE full-screen desktop gameplay UI concept for Last Chance Resort, in a closed futuristic volleyball arena. Wide landscape 16:10. A coherent game screen, not a presentation board.
Reference image: use ONLY for the indoor arena theme, teal/coral teams, gift drones, spring and porter hazards, side-view court. The user chose to KEEP THE GAME FULLY 2D. Completely redraw the reference in crisp FLAT 2D game art with readable user interface. Do not render photorealistic or 3D characters, 2.5D models, cinematic lighting or architectural perspective.
Visual style: clean hand-drawn / vector-like 2D indie game graphics, solid colour fills, thin outlines, at most two-tone cel shading, simplified recognizable adult human figures with articulated separate arms and legs for ragdoll animation. Clearly 2D. Midnight navy, slate-blue panels, cyan and coral-orange accents. Quiet low-detail environment, bright gameplay silhouettes. Typography is excellent clear sans serif with bold tabular score digits. Sparse intentional UI with comfortable spacing, easily implementable in HTML/CSS and Canvas.
Arena: enclosed future sports hall, a flat rear wall of large rectangular panels and repeating simple vertical supports, three understated cyan ceiling strips, short amber light marks. Orthographic straight side view with no vanishing point. Small flat side barriers and cyan/coral wall buttons. Thin horizontal court at y85%, a shallow bottom base, central edge-on net as a narrow upright at x50% from y85% to y61%. Game action occupies x8%-92%, y28%-85%.
Characters: man with dark hair and teal shorts at x33%, tumbling back in midair; woman ponytail and coral athletic outfit at x72% jumping to hit small yellow-blue-white volleyball at x62% y53%. Adult proportions simplified, body standing height about 19% frame. Two unmistakable flat 2D quadcopter sprites hover x23% y32% and x77% y32%, four rotor arms and discs, carrying a clearly separate ribboned gift below each body. Tiny lightning-bolt symbol on one gift indicates a power. Ground spring robot at x18%: orange base, simple visible steel coil and white cap. Wheeled express-porter hazard at x86%: ivory capsule, teal screen, two wheels, orange suitcase. All fully 2D, shapes easy to animate, no complicated machinery. Don't hide any playable element with UI.
UI layout:
1. Top-left compact DARK rounded score panel, thin muted cyan border: exact label "YOU", huge cyan digit "4", THREE small circular touch indicators below (two filled, one empty). At its bottom a tiny spring icon and exact text "SPRING · 8s".
2. Top-right symmetric score panel, muted coral border: exact label "CPU · LV 3", huge coral digit "3", THREE small touch indicators (one filled, two empty).
3. Top center a very compact row occupying only y4%-10%: small dark pill reading exact "NEXT: MAGNET" with a simple horseshoe magnet icon; three small rounded icon-only buttons for pause (two vertical bars), music (speaker), and fullscreen (four corners); pill reading exact "FIRST TO 10". These controls are visually distinct and have adequate spacing; no oversized floating holograms.
4. Directly under the center toolbar, tiny unobtrusive uppercase location text exactly "FUTURE ARENA". Keep main top center spacious.
5. Above the right side player's score-adjacent area, a small lightning icon with exact text "POWER · 18s", a slim short cyan progress bar showing 60%, placed within the top UI region rather than blocking the player.
6. Along the very bottom, a shallow dark footer separate from court, containing understated keyboard hint chips with exact texts "← → MOVE", "↑ JUMP", "SPACE SERVE", "P PAUSE". These are keyboard hints, NOT mobile touch controls. Align cleanly and leave generous gaps.
Make score and next-hazard readable first, then pause, then optional status details. All interface text ENGLISH and rendered accurately, no extra invented words.
Avoid: menu overlay, pause modal, browser frame, device mockup, infographic callouts, arrows explaining UI, multi-screen collage, artwork poster, touch joystick, mobile buttons, currencies, health bars, inventory, generic RPG UI, gradients pretending to be 3D, reflections, bloom, realistic skin, dense decorative details, too many boxes, any watermark.
